Approved evidence

DAYJOB

benchmark.dayjob

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Actual complete three creator-card and cross-domain harness-documentation reads establish one explicitly named DAYJOB benchmark family with finance/healthcare/tax domain manifestations, not three independent families. Primary source methods specify expert professional assignments, three-layer task review, Harbor packaging, restricted task networking and an agentic judge. Preserve source-version metric differences: finance/healthcare cards describe100percent criterion task-pass; tax describes95percent; current harness README averages dense rewards overfive attempts and excludes errored trials. No unqualified cross-source leaderboard comparison, global task total or score normalization is approved. Original five exact qualified observations have distinct actual author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts. MITcard metadata, evaluation-only/no-training requests and private/full-versus-public sample scopes remain attached; payloads/upstream rights/clinical or tax validity/judge calibration are unaudited. Full_source denotes complete available primary documentation, not professional-service or private-corpus validation.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

DAYJOB · access terms: The README specifies Harbor/OpenHands-based execution, an agent-phase allowlist for model API hosts and pinned OpenCode/rewardkit grading dependencies; cards reserve the tasks for held-out evaluation.

Permanent record ID: candidate.mandatory19.benchmark.dayjob.runtime-and-use-restrictions

  • Source-version-bound creator disclosure; private author-only candidate, with no approved scientific independence, new family coverage or supplier-relationship credit.
  • MIT card metadata coexists with explicit exclusion from training, distillation and checkpoint selection. Setup/grading network access is distinct from agent-phase access, and no provider APIs or paid runtime were used here.
